findings.headline: 5 accounts ($12,395,000 ARR) lost ~92% of usage within a day of each other, around 2026-05-22 (±1d)
findings.verdict: Likely upstream — one pipeline or metering change, not N churn events
evidence: 91 of 96 users kept running after the drop — the people did not leave
No error-rate spike in any account
Spans 4 verticals and 2 owners: building products, food distribution, healthcare services, restaurant franchising
Volume per account fell from 75 to 6 runs/day
findings.action: Check what shipped on this date (metering, export, quota) before opening churn plays. If it is real, it is a coordinated event worth one escalation.

findings.headline: 6 accounts ($11,225,000 ARR) have no activity export, but 6 of them still have users logging in
findings.verdict: Export gap, not dead accounts — do not read these as zero usage
evidence: 4.8 users logged in per account in the last 30 days, vs 5.5 for accounts that do have export files
Logins come from seat provisioning, a separate system from the activity export — so they are independent evidence
findings.action: Fix the export for these account IDs; until then their usage, error rate and adoption scores are unknown, not zero.
